item.description:
0.2.2 and 0.2.3 were never published, so this release carries all three: the 0.2.4 changes first, then 0.2.3's and 0.2.2's.

Accounts and sign-in

  • Sign in with a personal access token (classic or fine-grained) when an org blocks OAuth apps or needs SSO. A missing scope or an SSO block is named; a rejected token leaves the current sign-in untouched.
  • More than one GitHub account, with a switcher. Each account keeps its own Keychain item, and harborcli follows the active account and its host.
  • Downgrading after 0.2.4 starts you signed out: tokens moved from the shared item to one Keychain item per account.
  • Azure DevOps Connect works again. It asked for the user profile under dev.azure.com/{org}, where that API doesn't exist, so every token got "HTTP 404". A rejected token or an unknown organization is now named, and the token reaches the Keychain only after Azure accepts it.

Repos and local git

  • The repo picker suggests only your repos (yours, your orgs', ones you collaborate on). Tick "Include public repos" to search all of GitHub; those results always come after yours. A search with no match shows nothing instead of unrelated repos, and a slow, older search can't replace newer results.
  • Repos from every org you belong to and repos you collaborate on now show, not only orgs where you're an admin. Pinned repos outside the list are loaded.
  • Auto-sync is off by default, follows the fetch interval, and says "Synced" only when a branch actually moved.
  • Local git calls never wait on a prompt and stop after a timeout, so one stuck remote can't hang the refresh.
  • Each refresh enriches pinned repos and the 60 most recent others; the panel says when it stopped short.

Needs you and notifications

  • Your own pull requests appear in Needs you: checks failing, changes requested, conflicts, approved and green.
  • Harbor notifies once when something new lands in Needs you, never on first launch or sign-in, and can be switched off. The menu bar badge counts Tower's Needs you too.
  • The panel doesn't say "clear" until every search has answered.

Tower

  • In review fills from open pull requests, your global git ignore file is honoured, and each row says how old origin/main is.
  • Tower works without the agents ledger, and flags a worktree that has gone idle as "maybe waiting".

Keyboard, first run, VoiceOver

  • An optional global shortcut (⌃⌥H, off by default) and type-to-filter in the panel.
  • A short first run: sign in, pick folders, pin.
  • VoiceOver labels across the panel, the pull request pane and Tower.

From 0.2.3

Tower

  • A new Tower tab (⌘T) shows every agent worktree across your repos in lanes: Needs you, Working, Ready, In review, Leftovers. It reads the agents ledger and watches each repo's .git, so rows update within a second.
  • Each worktree gets a merge forecast against main. The forecast runs in a sandbox that can't write to your repos, never runs merge drivers, and says "couldn't check" instead of guessing. It needs git 2.41 or later.
  • Files changed in two or more live worktrees are flagged before either reaches main.
  • A retire queue lists worktrees the audit calls safe to remove, shows the dry run first, and asks before deleting. The panel stays open until it finishes.

Pull requests

  • A pull request pane says in plain words whether it can merge, and lets you resolve threads, update the branch and merge. The confirm names the branch it will delete, and is cancelled if the pull request changes while it is open.

Panel

  • Issues, pull requests, releases, runs and branches open as lists in the panel.
  • Sync, rebase and fast-forward a local clone from its repo detail.
  • Review requests appear in Needs you.
  • "All clear" appears only when every repository answered. Otherwise the panel says what it couldn't check, and the menu bar light turns into a hollow ring.
  • Clean up old workflow runs: keeps the newest 5 of every workflow, deletes one per second, stops on a rate limit, and has a Stop button.
  • Stars, forks and traffic in each repo; a year-by-month grid for All time.
  • More than one project folder.
  • A coloured menu bar icon and a new app icon.

Speed, without caches

  • Every cache is gone: no ETag store, no saved repo details, no "fetched recently" skips. Leftover cache files from earlier versions are removed.
  • Repository counts come from batched GraphQL queries. A refresh now makes 3 REST calls instead of about 330, and a cold refresh went from 7.0 s to 4.4 s.
  • GraphQL rate limits are recognised and back off, and the banner shows them.
  • Signing out or switching accounts clears everything from the old account at once.

Fixes

  • Upgrading no longer adds ~/Projects as a project folder you never chose.
  • Azure DevOps: opening the token help also opens your organization's token page.
  • CI actions are pinned to current versions, with Dependabot keeping them fresh.

From 0.2.2

Menu bar

  • Harbor's icon shows in the menu bar again, and clicking it opens the menu on macOS 27. Harbor now owns its status item directly instead of relying on a library that reached into private AppKit classes.
  • The icon is the Bollard template glyph: filled when calm, a corner dot and a count when a repository needs you, outline only when signed out.
  • Settings no longer opens on every launch for people who are signed in.

Themes

  • Six skins, under Settings → Menu → Look: Liquid Glass Native, Harbor Brand Navy, Ligne Claire Daylight, Ligne Claire Night Watch, Admiralty Chart and Signal Flags High Contrast. Each restyles the menu, heatmaps and Settings.
  • The Harbor view: your repositories as boats, moored when clean, listing with local drift, in a storm when CI fails, the tide showing two weeks of commits.

Real numbers

  • Each repository shows its open Dependabot alerts by severity, leaked secrets and code scanning alerts. Where GitHub won't say, Harbor says "unavailable", never zero. harborcli repo --security prints the same.
  • Traffic and forks appear in each repository's menu.
  • A failed pull request lookup no longer shows as 0 PRs, and "last refreshed" now means a refresh that finished.
  • harborcli repo --traffic, --heatmap and --release work; they were silently ignored.

Updates

  • Release notes of earlier versions stay in the update feed.

Credits

  • Harbor began as a fork of Peter Steinberger's RepoBar (MIT); the license and README now say so.

Sign-in

  • GitHub sign-in works again. 0.2.0 shipped with the ID of a retired OAuth app; Harbor now uses its new app, which needs no client secret.

CLI and polish

  • harborcli local --root with a folder that doesn't exist is an error, not "No repositories found".
  • Errors and help name the command harborcli.
  • The "stats are being generated" notice says Harbor, not a leftover name.

First signed release.

Sign-in and security

  • Sign in to GitHub with a one-time code at github.com/login/device. Harbor no longer ships an OAuth client secret. Your own OAuth app (e.g. GitHub Enterprise) still signs in through the browser.
  • Signing in can no longer get stuck on "Signing in…"; you can cancel it, and sign-in errors now show in the menu.
  • OAuth token responses are no longer written to the diagnostics log.
  • A GitHub Enterprise host typed without https:// (ghe.example.com) now works; an unusable host shows an error instead of quietly signing in to github.com.

Azure DevOps

  • Work-item queries are valid WIQL: "is one of" filters, area and iteration paths with backslashes, tag filters, and the first condition of a query.
  • Project filters now filter by project, and "last N days" / stale-item queries use N instead of today.
  • Commit change counts show up.

CLI

  • harborcli help and messages use the Harbor name throughout.

Look

  • New app icon: a mooring bollard with a yellow line made fast around it.

Security

  • Every secret (GitHub tokens, OAuth app credentials, Azure DevOps PATs, GitLab tokens) is kept in the macOS Keychain through one store, local to your Mac and never synced to iCloud.
  • Listing Azure DevOps organizations no longer fails when a PAT is saved.
  • All known dependency vulnerabilities fixed.

Local Git

  • A missing git or a folder that isn't a repository is reported as such, not as "uncommitted changes".

Packaging

  • Developer ID signed, notarized, hardened runtime; Sparkle updates from github.com/sriinnu/harbor; Homebrew cask sriinnu/tap/harbor installs the app and the harborcli command.
